name: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
credit: The Tyrannicides, Harmodius and Aristogeiton (statue group), glass lantern slide, photographer unknown, Université de Louvain collection (KU Leuven) · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: The Attic scolia are the drinking-songs of Athenian banqueting, sung at the symposium by guests who passed a myrtle branch or a lyre from couch to couch, each taking up a short song in turn. They are anonymous, brief and sung from memory: hymns to Athena, Demeter, Leto and Pan, maxims about friendship and health, wishes to be a lyre or a jewel, and a warning about the scorpion under every stone.

The collection survives in the fifteenth book of Athenaeus, which quotes some two dozen of them in a fixed order. Its best-known members are the songs on Harmodius and Aristogeiton, the tyrannicides of 514 BC, one of which is traditionally ascribed to Callistratus; a few songs carry other names (Simonides, Alcaeus, Praxilla). The Greek is given here from Bergk’s Anthologia lyrica of 1868, collated with the 1904 Hiller-Crusius edition, with J. M. Edmonds’s English of 1927.

poems.title: Scolion 2: Παλλὰς Τριτογένειʼ, ἄνασσʼ Ἀθάνα
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Παλλὰς Τριτογένειʼ, ἄνασσʼ Ἀθάνα,
ὄρθου τήνδε πόλιν τε καὶ πολίτας
ἄτερ ἀλγέων καὶ στάσεων
καὶ θανάτων ἀώρων, σύ τε καὶ πατήρ.

poems.title: Scolion 3: Πλούτου μητέρʼ Ὀλυμπίαν ἀείδω
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Πλούτου μητέρʼ Ὀλυμπίαν ἀείδω
Δήμητρα στεφανηφόροις ἐν ὥραις,
σέ τε, παῖ Διός, Φερσεφόνη·
χαίρετον, εὖ δὲ τήνδʼ ἀμφιέπετον πόλιν.

poems.title: Scolion 4: Ἐν Δήλῳ ποτʼ ἔτικτε τέκνα Λατώ
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ἐν Δήλῳ ποτʼ ἔτικτε τέκνα Λατώ,
Φοῖβον χρυσοκόμαν, ἄνακτʼ Ἀπόλλω,
ἐλαφηβόλον τʼ ἀγροτέραν
Ἄρτεμιν, ἃ γυναικῶν μέγʼ ἔχει κράτος.

poems.title: Scolion 5: Ὦ Πάν, Ἀρκαδίας μέδων κλεεννᾶς
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ὦ Πάν, Ἀρκαδίας μέδων κλεεννᾶς,
ὀρχηστὰ βρομίαις ὀπαδὲ Νύμφαις,
γελάσαις, ὦ Πάν, ἐπʼ ἐμαῖς
εὐφροσύναισι ταῖσδʼ ἀοιδαῖς κεχαρημένος.

poems.title: Scolion 6: Ἐνικήσαμεν ὡς ἐβουλόμεσθα
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ἐνικήσαμεν ὡς ἐβουλόμεσθα,
καὶ νίκην ἔδοσαν θεοὶ φέροντες
παρὰ Πανδρόσου ὡς φίλην Ἀθηνᾶν.

poems.title: Scolion 7: Εἴθʼ ἐξῆν, ὁποῖός τις ἦν ἕκαστος
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Εἴθʼ ἐξῆν, ὁποῖός τις ἦν ἕκαστος,
τὸ στῆθος διελόντʼ, ἔπειτα τὸν νοῦν
ἐσιδόντα, κλείσαντα πάλιν,
ἄνδρα φίλον νομίζειν ἀδόλῳ φρενί.

poems.title: Scolion 8: Ὑγιαίνειν μὲν ἄριστον ἀνδρὶ θνατῷ
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.note: Ascribed to Simonides (by others to Epicharmus).
poems.text:
Ὑγιαίνειν μὲν ἄριστον ἀνδρὶ θνατῷ,
δεύτερον δὲ φυὰν καλὸν γενέσθαι,
τὸ τρίτον δὲ πλουτεῖν ἀδόλως,
καὶ τὸ τέταρτον ἡβᾶν μετὰ τῶν φίλων.

poems.title: Scolion 9: Ἐν μύρτου κλαδὶ τὸ ξίφος φορήσω
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.note: Ascribed to Callistratus; one of the songs on Harmodius and Aristogeiton, who killed the tyrant Hipparchus in 514 BC.
poems.text:
Ἐν μύρτου κλαδὶ τὸ ξίφος φορήσω,
ὥσπερ Ἁρμόδιος καὶ Ἀριστογείτων,
ὅτε τὸν τύραννον κτανέτην
ἰσονόμους τʼ Ἀθήνας ἐποιησάτην.

poems.title: Scolion 10: Φίλταθʼ Ἁρμόδιʼ, οὔ τί που τέθνηκας
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.note: One of the songs on Harmodius and Aristogeiton.
poems.text:
Φίλταθʼ Ἁρμόδιʼ, οὔ τί που τέθνηκας,
νήσοις δʼ ἐν μακάρων σέ φασιν εἶναι,
ἵνα περ ποδώκης Ἀχιλεύς,
Τυδεΐδην τέ φασιν ἐσθλὸν Διομήδεα.

poems.title: Scolion 11: Ἐν μύρτου κλαδὶ τὸ ξίφος φορήσω
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.note: One of the songs on Harmodius and Aristogeiton.
poems.text:
Ἐν μύρτου κλαδὶ τὸ ξίφος φορήσω,
ὥσπερ Ἁρμόδιος καὶ Ἀριστογείτων,
ὅτʼ Ἀθηναίης ἐν θυσίαις
ἄνδρα τύραννον Ἵππαρχον ἐκαινέτην.

poems.title: Scolion 12: Αἰεὶ σφῷν κλέος ἔσσεται κατʼ αἶαν
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.note: One of the songs on Harmodius and Aristogeiton.
poems.text:
Αἰεὶ σφῷν κλέος ἔσσεται κατʼ αἶαν,
φίλταθʼ Ἁρμόδιε καὶ Ἀριστογείτων,
ὅτι τὸν τύραννον κτανέτην
ἰσονόμους τʼ Ἀθήνας ἐποιησάτην.

poems.title: Scolion 14: Αἰαῖ Λειψύδριον προδωσέταιρον
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Αἰαῖ Λειψύδριον προδωσέταιρον,
οἵους ἄνδρας ἀπώλεσας, μάχεσθαι
ἀγαθούς τε καὶ εὐπατρίδας,
οἳ τότʼ ἔδειξαν οἵων πατέρων ἔσαν.

poems.title: Scolion 15: Ἐκ γῆς χρὴ κατιδεῖν πλόον
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ἐκ γῆς χρὴ κατιδεῖν πλόον,
εἴ τις δύναιτο καὶ παλάμην ἔχοι·
ἐπεὶ δέ κʼ ἐν πόντῳ γένηται,
τῷ παρεόντι τρέχειν ἀνάγκη.

poems.title: Scolion 16: Ὁ καρκίνος ὧδʼ ἔφα
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ὁ καρκίνος ὧδʼ ἔφα
χαλᾷ τὸν ὄφιν λαβών·
“εὐθὺν χρὴ τὸν ἑταῖρον ἔμμεν
καὶ μὴ σκολιὰ φρονεῖν.”

poems.title: Scolion 17: Παῖ Τελαμῶνος, Αἶαν αἰχμητά, λέγουσί σε
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Παῖ Τελαμῶνος, Αἶαν αἰχμητά, λέγουσί σε
ἐς Τροΐαν ἄριστον ἐλθεῖν Δαναῶν μετʼ Ἀχιλλέα.

poems.title: Scolion 18: Τὸν Τελαμῶνα πρῶτον, Αἴαντα δὲ δεύτερον
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Τὸν Τελαμῶνα πρῶτον, Αἴαντα δὲ δεύτερον
ἐς Τροΐαν λέγουσιν ἐλθεῖν Δαναῶν μετʼ Ἀχιλλέα.

poems.title: Scolion 19: Εἴθε λύρα καλὴ γενοίμην ἐλεφαντίνη
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Εἴθε λύρα καλὴ γενοίμην ἐλεφαντίνη,
καί με καλοὶ παῖδες φέροιεν Διονύσιον ἐς χορόν.

poems.title: Scolion 20: Εἴθʼ ἄπυρον καλὸν γενοίμην μέγα χρυσίον
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Εἴθʼ ἄπυρον καλὸν γενοίμην μέγα χρυσίον,
καί με καλὴ γυνὴ φοροίη καθαρὸν θεμένη νόον.

poems.title: Scolion 21: Ἀδμήτου λόγον, ὦ ʼταῖρε, μαθὼν τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς φίλει
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ἀδμήτου λόγον, ὦ ʼταῖρε, μαθὼν τοὺς ἀγαθοὺς φίλει·
τῶν δειλῶν δʼ ἀπέχου, γνοὺς ὅτι δειλοῖς ὀλίγα χάρις.

poems.title: Scolion 22: Σὺν μοι πῖνε, συνήβα, συνέρα, συστεφανηφόρει
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Σὺν μοι πῖνε, συνήβα, συνέρα, συστεφανηφόρει,
σὺν μοι μαινομένῳ μαίνεο, σὺν σώφρονι σωφρόνει.

poems.title: Scolion 23: Ὑπὸ παντὶ λίθῳ σκορπίος, ὦ ʼταῖρʼ, ὑποδύεται
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ὑπὸ παντὶ λίθῳ σκορπίος, ὦ ʼταῖρʼ, ὑποδύεται·
φράζευ, μή σε βάλῃ· τῷ δʼ ἀφανεῖ πᾶς ἕπεται δόλος.

poems.title: Scolion 24: Ἁ ὗς τὰν βάλανον τὰν μὲν ἔχει, τὰν δʼ ἔραται λαβεῖν
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ἁ ὗς τὰν βάλανον τὰν μὲν ἔχει, τὰν δʼ ἔραται λαβεῖν·
κἀγὼ παῖδα καλὴν τὴν μὲν ἔχω, τὴν δʼ ἔραμαι λαβεῖν.

poems.title: Scolion 25: Πόρνα καὶ βαλανεὺς τωὐτὸν ἔχουσʼ ἐμπεδέως ἔθος
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Πόρνα καὶ βαλανεὺς τωὐτὸν ἔχουσʼ ἐμπεδέως ἔθος·
ἐν ταὐτᾷ πυέλῳ τόν τʼ ἀγαθὸν τόν τε κακὸν λόει.

poems.title: Scolion 26: Ὅστις ἄνδρα φίλον μὴ προδίδωσιν, μεγάλαν ἔχει
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ὅστις ἄνδρα φίλον μὴ προδίδωσιν, μεγάλαν ἔχει
τιμὰν ἔν τε βροτοῖς ἔν τε θεοῖσιν κατʼ ἐμὸν νόον.

poems.title: Scolion 27: Ἔγχει καὶ Κήδωνι, διάκονε, μηδʼ ἐπιλήθου
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Anthologia lyrica (Bergk, 1868): Scolia
poems.text:
Ἔγχει καὶ Κήδωνι, διάκονε, μηδʼ ἐπιλήθου,
εἰ δὴ χρὴ ἀγαθοῖς ἀνδράσιν οἰνοχοεῖν.

poems.title: Scolion 2 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Trito-born Pallas, Queen Athena, uphold thou this City and her people, thou and thy Father, without pains or strifes or untimely deaths.

poems.title: Scolion 3 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Thee O bountiful Demeter, mother of Wealth, I sing at the wearing of the wreath, and with thee Persephoné daughter of Zeus; all hail, ye twain, and protect this City.

poems.title: Scolion 4 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: In Delos of yore did Leto bear children twain, Phoebus the golden-haired, Lord Apollo, and Huntress Artemis shooter of deer, who holdeth so great sway over women.

poems.title: Scolion 5 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: O Pan, thou Lord of famed Arcadia, comrade-dancer of the rioting Nymphs, mayst thou smile, ho Pan! with pleasure at these my merry songs.

poems.title: Scolion 6 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: We have won as we wished, and the Gods have given victory [for the sake of Cecropian] Pandrosus and her friend Athena [upholder of cities].

poems.title: Scolion 7 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Would it were possible to part every breast and so read the mind within, and then closing it up believe beyond all doubt the man is a friend.

poems.title: Scolion 8 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.note: Edmonds numbers this song 7. For this song Edmonds prints Robert Herrick’s seventeenth-century version.

poems.title: Scolion 9 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.note: Edmonds prints the four Harmodius songs together as his no. 10; the English is split here to match the Greek.
poems.text: I’ll carry my sword in a myrtle-branch, like Harmodius and Aristogeiton when they slew the despot and made Athens free.

poems.title: Scolion 10 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.note: Edmonds prints the four Harmodius songs together as his no. 10; the English is split here to match the Greek.
poems.text: Dearest Harmodius, I know thou art not dead, because they tell me thou art in the Islands of the Blest, where Achilles lives still, and brave Diomed.

poems.title: Scolion 11 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.note: Edmonds prints the four Harmodius songs together as his no. 10; the English is split here to match the Greek.
poems.text: I’ll carry my sword in a myrtle-branch, like Harmodius and Aristogeiton when at the Feast of Athena they killed the despot Hipparchus.

poems.title: Scolion 12 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.note: Edmonds prints the four Harmodius songs together as his no. 10; the English is split here to match the Greek.
poems.text: Your fame shall live in the earth for ever, dearest Harmodius and Aristogeiton, how you slew the despot and made Athens free.

poems.title: Scolion 14 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Alas thou betrayer of friends, Leipsydrium, what heroes thou hast slain—gallant soldiers and high-born gentlemen who then did show of what lineage they came.

poems.title: Scolion 15 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: A mariner should view his course from the shore, if he but have the power and skill; but once he is on the sea he must run before whatever wind may blow.

poems.title: Scolion 16 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Said the Crab when he clawed the Snake, “A friend should be straight and not be crooked-hearted.”

poems.title: Scolion 17 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Son of Telamon, spearman Aias, men say that next to Achilles thou wast the noblest Greek that ever went to Troy.

poems.title: Scolion 18 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Men say that Telamon was first, and Aias second, after Achilles, of all the Greeks that went to Troy.

poems.title: Scolion 19 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: O would I might become a pretty ivory lyre, and pretty lads might take me with them to Dionysus’ choral dance.

poems.title: Scolion 20 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: O would I might become a pretty great new gold jewel, and a pretty woman might wear me with a mind pure of ill.

poems.title: Scolion 21 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Learn the tale of Admetus, my friend, and seek acquaintance of the brave; but from the coward hold thee aloof, since there’s little gratitude in such as he.

poems.title: Scolion 22 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: Drink with me, play with me, love with me, be wreathed with me; be wild when I am wild, and when I am staid be staid.

poems.title: Scolion 23 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: ’Neath every stone, friend, lurks a scorpion; beware or he’ll sting you; for there’s no treachery but waits upon the unseen.

poems.title: Scolion 24 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: This acorn the sow has, that, she is fain to have; and this fair maid I have, that, I am fain to have.

poems.title: Scolion 25 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text:
’Twixt harlot and bathman the likeness is pat;
Both wash good and bad in the very same vat.

poems.title: Scolion 26 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: The man who betrays not his friend hath great honour methinks both of men and of Gods.

poems.title: Scolion 27 (Edmonds)
poems.author: Attic Scolia (Anonymous)
poems.collection: Lyra Graeca, vol. III (Loeb, 1927): Attic Scolia
poems.text: If good men deserve a drink, drawer, forget thou not to pour one out for Cedon.
